svg.title: [HTTP binding] MCP mid-interaction authorization over Streamable HTTP 401 insufficient_authorization + RAR remediation, one-shot token bound to ONE operation (CHALLENGE_BINDING=http, default)

g.text: [HTTP binding] MCP mid-interaction authorization over Streamable HTTP
401 insufficient_authorization + RAR remediation, one-shot token bound to ONE operation (CHALLENGE_BINDING=http, default)
1. Transfer: the tool discovers it needs a per-operation grant
3. Challenge: "authorization required" for op_X (atomic: nothing committed)
stepUpFetch HOLDS request id=7; the LLM and the MCP SDK see nothing yet
4. Client remediation: ONE-SHOT token for op_X
op_X stays awaiting_authorization until TTL -> failed.
5. Retry with T2: resolve by token, claim atomically, commit once
6. Later calls keep using the SESSION token
token presented on ANOTHER operation with identical values
request id=9 is a second identical transfer -> its own op_Y (instruction_id op_Y)
one-shot token on a non-payment tool
8. Guard: challenge after a side effect (non-atomic tool)
With known payees nothing is committed first: one challenge carries N details
(instruction_id op_B-1 … op_B-N), so one consent and one token cover the batch.
• Tools never advertise the requirement; it is discovered during execution.
• HTTP binding: 401 insufficient_authorization leaves the JSON-RPC request unanswered, so the client replays the SAME id.
The in-band (stream) binding is in stepup-stream.puml.
• authorization_details carry instruction_id = the server's operation id: a grant authorizes ONE operation instance.
• Claim = executing + jti spent, atomically, before any side effect; completed operations return their stored result.
• Operation token: authorization_details only, NO scope, short TTL, no refresh. Session token (mcp:basic) is never replaced.
• A refusal is a tool result (isError), not a transport error. Elicitation is UX, never the authorization itself.
• Open gap: the AS cannot verify the RS issued the instruction_id (a server-signed remediation would close it).
